text: For the broad AI theme, the first-pass US-listed universe should be organized into demand engines (hyperscalers), compute (GPU/ASIC/foundry), networking, infrastructure power/cooling, and adjacent software layers.
Likely scarce nodes to investigate next are AI accelerators, leading-edge foundry/packaging, high-speed networking, data-center power/cooling, and grid/electrical equipment.
Next layer should add memory/HBM, advanced packaging, photonics, test equipment, and selected AI software/application names to reduce blind spots.

For AI, the highest-priority layers remain accelerators, advanced packaging/foundry, networking, and data-center power/cooling; hyperscalers are the demand engines rather than the bottleneck themselves.
Power and thermal management are emerging as a real chokepoint because higher rack density and liquid-cooling requirements can slow deployment even when compute supply is available.
AI networking is a separate bottleneck from compute; large-cluster rollouts require switch fabrics and Ethernet gear that can gate deployment timing.
Hyperscaler capex guidance and AI chip deployment announcements remain the fastest-moving catalysts for this theme and should be checked every earnings cycle.
Memory/HBM, advanced packaging subcontractors, photonics, and test/inspection equipment are under-covered and should be searched next with primary-source evidence.
For Layer 3 AI ranking, prioritize the most structurally scarce upstream control points first: accelerators, foundry/advanced packaging, networking, and data-center power/cooling.
Memory/HBM, advanced packaging subcontractors, photonics, and test/inspection equipment remain under-covered and should be added in the next research pass.
Hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta are demand engines rather than bottleneck suppliers; they are useful for validation but should usually rank below scarce-layer suppliers.
For Layer 4 AI, prioritize direct chokepoints first: accelerators, foundry/advanced packaging, and lithography; keep hyperscalers lower because they mainly validate demand rather than control supply.
Next-pass candidates should include HBM/memory, advanced packaging subcontractors, photonics, and test/inspection equipment, since these may be under-covered but important AI bottlenecks.

For Layer 5 AI, the highest-value follow-on deep research target is TSMC because it links leading-edge foundry capacity and advanced packaging into a single scarce control point for AI accelerator scaling.

The next verification step should focus on live primary sources: current utilization, CoWoS/advanced-packaging capacity, customer reservation, backlog, and capex guidance to test whether the bottleneck is still binding.
